question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=6-3x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3\,⟹\,-\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $3$ | $0$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}2\cdot {3}^{6-3x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{0}2\cdot {3}^{u}(-\frac{1}{3})\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{3}^{0}{3}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}(\frac{{3}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}){|}_{3}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3}({3}^{0}-{3}^{3}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(1-27) \\  & =\frac{52}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$
